emberglow.1: A lamplighter on a ladder stops mid-wick and asks if any of you have seen his apprentice; the boy went into Kettlewhistle at dusk and the lamps there are still dark.
emberglow.2: An airship shuttle groans overhead between the masts, and a single glove drifts down from its gondola, still warm.
emberglow.3: Two Wickguard argue over a body at a canal lock, each insisting it floated in from the other's ward.
emberglow.4: A Solar Conclave crier reads out the week's debts by name from the steps of a bank, and the crowd goes quiet when he reaches a name one of you knows.
emberglow.5: Steam pours from a grating in the street, smelling of cabbage, ink and something sweeter underneath.
emberglow.6: A child sells paper suns on sticks for a copper each, promising they keep the dark away for one night only.
emberglow.7: A shuttered shop has a fresh sign in the window: "Closed until the light returns." Someone has scratched "never" beneath it.
emberglow.8: The bells of the Temple Borough ring the hour one stroke short, and every head in the street turns.
emberglow.9: A barge drifts down the canal with no one at the tiller, its lantern lit and its cargo hidden under oilcloth.
emberglow.10: A Warden kneels in the gutter planting weeds between the cobbles, humming, and asks you to hold her trowel for a moment.
emberglow.11: A brass band rehearses behind a warehouse door, playing the same four bars over and over, each time a little slower.
emberglow.12: Rain sheets off the rooftops in grey ropes, and a dozen strangers crowd under the same narrow awning as you, all pretending not to listen to each other.
emberglow.13: A gentleman in an immaculate coat drops a purse, glances at you, and walks on without picking it up.
emberglow.14: A queue of people stretches round the block outside the Bakers' Hall; the bread inside is stamped with a mark nobody recognises.
emberglow.15: A broadsheet seller cries the news of a murder in the Highrise, and the drawing on the front looks very much like one of you.
emberglow.16: Gaslight hisses along a crooked lane, and every third lamp has been painted black from the inside.
emberglow.17: A fortune-teller's parrot calls out a name from its cage as you pass; its owner covers the cage quickly and apologises.
emberglow.18: Two guild apprentices are fighting with sticks in an alley over whose master has the older charter; they stop to ask you to judge.
emberglow.19: A clockmaker's window is full of clocks, all stopped at the same minute.
emberglow.20: Washing hangs between the tenements so thickly that the street below is lit only in strips, like light through a cage.
emberglow.21: A woman leans from a high window and lowers a basket on a rope, calling down for someone to fill it with whatever they can spare.
emberglow.22: An old soldier with a tin leg plays a hurdy-gurdy on a corner, and the tune is a marching song from a war no one talks about.
emberglow.23: A crowd gathers to watch a building being pulled down; a cheer goes up as the front wall falls, revealing a room no one knew was there.
emberglow.24: The air near the Guildforge tastes of iron, and the cobbles are warm through your boots.
emberglow.25: A funeral procession files past in total silence, every mourner carrying an unlit candle.
emberglow.26: A pamphleteer presses a sheet into your hand, urging a general strike, then hurries away as a Wickguard patrol rounds the corner.
emberglow.27: A cat sits on a windowsill eating a fish larger than itself, glaring at anyone who looks too long.
emberglow.28: Children dare each other to touch the door of a boarded-up house, then scatter shrieking before anyone reaches it.
emberglow.29: A Flux-Weaver in a stained robe walks past muttering sums, a faint smell of ozone trailing behind her.
emberglow.30: The canal smells of tar and rot, and something large moves lazily beneath the surface near the lock gates.
emberglow.31: A street of tanners hangs hides from every balcony, and the stench drives even the rats to the other side of the road.
emberglow.32: A carriage with a noble crest has stopped in the middle of the street, and the driver is asleep with the reins in his lap.
emberglow.33: A night-soil cart rumbles by, and the driver greets everyone he passes by name, including you, though you have never met.
emberglow.34: A shop sells nothing but locks, and the shopkeeper asks what you have to keep safe before he will let you browse.
emberglow.35: The steam whistle of a manufactory shrieks, and a tide of workers pours out of its gates, faces grey with dust.
emberglow.36: On a church step, a priest of the House of the Many is scrubbing at a word painted on the door that keeps showing through the whitewash.
emberglow.37: A herald of the Council of Many nails a new ordinance to a post: all lamps must now be registered and taxed.
emberglow.38: A lost child sits on the kerb, perfectly calm, and says her mother told her to wait for "the ones with the road on their boots".
emberglow.39: A pie seller swears his pies are pork, and his dog, sitting beside the cart, looks away.
emberglow.40: A man on stilts walks above the crowd handing out cards for the Sinful Folly, and winks at one of you as if you were an old friend.
emberglow.41: Fog from the Gaslake rolls up the streets so thickly that the gas-lamps become floating smudges of yellow.
emberglow.42: A row of rented rooms advertises "Light included", and a long queue waits to see what that means.
emberglow.43: A grand ball is under way in a lit mansion on the Bluff, and the music drifts down to the street where a crowd stands in the cold to listen.
emberglow.44: A scavenger back from the Hinterlands is selling relics from a blanket, and one of them is humming softly.
emberglow.45: A dog runs past with a human hand in its mouth, chased by a butcher shouting that it is only wax.
emberglow.46: An old woman stops you to ask the date, and when told, she weeps and thanks you.
emberglow.47: A banner stretched across the street announces the Radiant Abbot's visit, and someone has set a tiny noose on its central sun.
emberglow.48: Boys fish from a bridge with string and bent pins, and every one of them has caught the same small, eyeless fish.
emberglow.49: A bookbinder's shop has a window of beautiful volumes with no titles, and a notice reading "Your story, bound, ten shillings".
emberglow.50: A procession of debtors in chains is led towards the Conclave's workhouse, and one of them catches your eye and mouths a single word: "Help."
emberglow.51: Smoke from a hundred chimneys hangs flat over the rooftops, and somewhere above it, the sun is a coin seen through dirty water.
emberglow.52: A tavern sign creaks above you showing a lantern with a hand clutching it; laughter and the smell of cabbee spill from inside.
emberglow.53: A man paints the same street scene every day on the same corner, and today he has painted you into it.
emberglow.54: A cart overturns at a crossing and spills a load of oranges, and the whole street drops everything to grab what it can.
emberglow.55: A widow in black stands at a tram stop holding a birdcage with the door open and no bird.
emberglow.56: A fresh poster on a wall offers a reward for "information on the lights seen over Riverview", signed by the Second Directorate.
emberglow.57: The ring of hammers from Brannoc's forge carries for streets, and a boy runs past carrying a sword wrapped in sacking.
emberglow.58: A choir practises in an empty market hall, their voices echoing in the iron rafters long after they stop.
emberglow.59: A gutter runs bright red, and a nearby dyer shouts that it is only madder before anyone can ask.
emberglow.60: A flock of pigeons bursts up from a square all at once, though nothing seems to have startled them.
emberglow.61: A beggar wears a coat of real ermine, worn to threads, and will not say where he got it.
emberglow.62: Two lovers quarrel on a bridge in a language none of you recognise, then kiss, then quarrel again.
emberglow.63: A clerk runs past with an armful of ledgers, drops one, and does not stop; it lies open on a page full of names crossed out in red.
emberglow.64: The street narrows to a stairway cut through the old city wall, its steps worn into deep bowls by centuries of feet.
emberglow.65: An undertaker measures a man who is still alive and arguing about the price.
emberglow.66: A puppet show in a doorway tells the story of the Gloaming, and the children watching it are utterly silent.
emberglow.67: Someone has chalked a map of the city on the paving stones, with one district left blank and marked "here be nothing".
emberglow.68: A lone airship mast stands unused at the end of a lane, its mooring lines cut and swaying.
emberglow.69: A street vendor fries dough in a cauldron of oil, and the warmth from it draws a ring of shivering people.
emberglow.70: A fine lady's carriage splashes through a puddle and drenches a line of washerwomen, who curse it in perfect harmony.
emberglow.71: A man is selling "genuine sunlight" in corked bottles, and a crowd argues over whether the glow is real.
emberglow.72: A row of statues in a square has been beheaded, and someone has placed turnips in their place.
emberglow.73: A boy on the corner sings out the prices from the corn exchange; they have doubled since yesterday.
emberglow.74: A heavy door in an alley opens a crack, a pale hand beckons, and it shuts again before you reach it.
emberglow.75: Every window in one tall house is lit with a single candle, and a sign on the door reads "Vigil. Do not knock."
emberglow.76: A brewer's dray clatters by with its barrels steaming, and the horses wear blinkers stitched with suns.
emberglow.77: A street sweeper pauses to show you a coin he found in the gutter: it bears the face of a king no one remembers.
emberglow.78: A press-gang of the levy works the crowd, asking young men if they would like to see the Hinterlands, all expenses paid.
emberglow.79: Laughter Lane is quiet for once; every painted door is shut, and a single carnival mask lies in the road.
emberglow.80: A gondolier on the canal sings an old love song, and stops dead when his pole strikes something under the water.
emberglow.81: A bonfire of old furniture burns in a courtyard while the tenants dance round it in their nightclothes.
emberglow.82: An apothecary's window displays jars of leeches, a two-headed lamb in spirits, and a notice offering a cure for "the Fade".
emberglow.83: A procession of Solar Prelates passes under parasols of gold leaf, and the crowd bows by habit and spits once they have gone.
emberglow.84: Hammering echoes from inside a shuttered chapel, and a sign on the door says "Closed for consecration".
emberglow.85: A guard dog strains at its chain outside a moneylender's, barking at something in the empty doorway opposite.
emberglow.86: A girl hands out white ribbons on behalf of the Grand Matriarch, and asks each passer-by to tie one on their sleeve "for when the strike comes".
emberglow.87: The tide of the Gaslake has gone out further than anyone remembers, leaving boats tilted in the mud along the waterfront.
emberglow.88: A tea-house window is crowded with old men playing a board game whose pieces are all carved as little lanterns.
emberglow.89: A street magician makes a coin vanish from your palm, and does not seem able to make it come back.
emberglow.90: A house on the corner is being repainted, and the painters are covering a large, faded mural of an angel made of ash.
emberglow.91: Someone has left a bunch of fresh wildflowers on a doorstep in the middle of the city, and no one will touch them.
emberglow.92: A runaway horse thunders down the street dragging an empty cab, and the crowd parts like water.
emberglow.93: A Wickguard sergeant pins a "Wanted" bill to a post, then stands back and squints at it as though he is not sure who he is looking for.
emberglow.94: A bakery's ovens have gone cold, and the baker sits in the doorway telling anyone who will listen that the fire simply would not catch.
emberglow.95: A crowd watches a tightrope walker cross between two chimneys high above the street, holding a lantern in each hand.
emberglow.96: Bells, whistles and the cries of a thousand traders rise around you, and for a moment the whole city sounds like one living thing.
emberglow.97: A knife-grinder's wheel shrieks on a street corner, and every cook in the lane queues with a blade in hand, swapping gossip about the Conclave.
emberglow.98: A doorway in the Spindlecore is painted with fresh chalk marks: a sun, a crescent and a hand, and the family inside will not explain them.
emberglow.99: A rich man's funeral carriage is drawn by six black horses with plumes, and street urchins race behind it hoping for scattered coins.
emberglow.100: High on a rooftop, a woman is feeding a flock of crows from her apron, and every one of them falls silent to watch you pass.

heartlands.1: Wheat stands golden to the horizon, and a scarecrow in a Conclave tabard seems to turn its head to follow you.
heartlands.2: At a wayshrine to Sol, someone has left a loaf, a knife and a note that reads "for whoever needs it more".
heartlands.3: A tithe-cart has lost a wheel in the road, and the driver begs for help before the Conclave's riders count the grain and find it short.
heartlands.4: Larks rise from the stubble ahead of you, and for a moment the sun feels almost warm.
heartlands.5: A village is holding a wedding in a barn, and the bride's father insists that strangers at a wedding bring luck: you must come in and dance.
heartlands.6: An old milestone has been recarved, and the distance to Emberglow is now longer than it was.
heartlands.7: Children chase a goose down the lane with sticks, and the goose seems to be winning.
heartlands.8: A Solar Prelate's glass carriage passes with its blinds drawn, and the field-hands kneel in the dust until it is out of sight.
heartlands.9: Beehives line a hedgerow, every one of them silent; the beekeeper sits among them with her veil in her lap, weeping.
heartlands.10: Smoke rises straight up from a cottage chimney into a still sky, and someone inside is baking bread.
heartlands.11: A shepherd counts his flock through a gate and frowns: there is one more sheep than he owns.
heartlands.12: The road runs between two rows of poplars planted so exactly that they seem to go on forever.
heartlands.13: A miller waves you over and asks you to settle a bet: does his waterwheel turn backwards at night, or is his wife teasing him?
heartlands.14: A harvest crew sings as it scythes, and the song changes to a mocking verse about travellers as you pass.
heartlands.15: A ploughman has stopped mid-furrow and stands staring at something his blade has turned up: a bronze helm, green with age.
heartlands.16: An inn sign shows a sheaf of wheat with a sun behind it, and the landlord stands at the door with arms folded, sizing you up.
heartlands.17: A pedlar's wagon is drawn up by a ford, selling ribbons, pins, needles and gossip from three villages back.
heartlands.18: A small girl offers you a cup of water from the well and asks, very seriously, whether you have been to the edge of the world.
heartlands.19: A field has been burned black in a perfect circle, and the farmer swears it was not him.
heartlands.20: Swallows skim low over a pond, and an old man fishing there says that means the weather will turn.
heartlands.21: A chapel bell rings for a burial, and the whole village follows a tiny coffin up the hill.
heartlands.22: A Conclave tax-collector sits at a folding table by the road with two armed men, stopping every traveller to ask what they carry.
heartlands.23: An orchard's apples have all fallen at once, carpeting the grass red, and the trees stand bare in midsummer.
heartlands.24: A farm dog trots alongside you for a mile, then sits at a boundary stone and will go no further.
heartlands.25: A family is moving house on a hay cart piled with furniture, children and chickens, singing as they go.
heartlands.26: A great oak stands alone in a field, hung with hundreds of tiny clay suns on threads that click in the wind.
heartlands.27: A haywain blocks the lane, and its driver is fast asleep under his hat while his horse eats the hedge.
heartlands.28: A man in a field is digging a hole, and when you ask what it is for, he says, "For later."
heartlands.29: A wayside cross has been decorated with corn dollies, each one with a little face drawn in soot.
heartlands.30: Two farmers argue over a stone wall that one of them says moved a foot in the night.
heartlands.31: A string of Conclave pilgrims passes, barefoot and singing, their feet bloody, their faces shining.
heartlands.32: The air smells of cut hay and woodsmoke, and somewhere a cow is lowing as if it has lost something.
heartlands.33: An abandoned scythe stands upright in the middle of a half-cut field, as if its owner simply walked away.
heartlands.34: A village pump has a queue of women with buckets, and they fall silent when you come near.
heartlands.35: A boy flies a kite shaped like a sun, and the string runs up into the clouds out of sight.
heartlands.36: At a crossroads, someone has buried a dead dog and marked the grave with a carefully painted board.
heartlands.37: A bridge troll in a Conclave toll-keeper's coat, or perhaps just a very ugly man, asks for a penny each to cross.
heartlands.38: A woman spreads linen on a hedge to bleach in the thin sun and calls out to ask whether it will rain where you are going.
heartlands.39: A herd of cattle is driven past, branded with the Radiant Abbot's sun, and the drovers will not meet anyone's eye.
heartlands.40: A merchant's coach has stopped at the roadside, and inside a fine lady is reading aloud to a frightened little dog.
heartlands.41: Stubble fires smoulder in the distance, and the low sun turns the smoke the colour of copper.
heartlands.42: A wandering tinker mends a kettle by the road, singing about a town that sank into the earth for its pride.
heartlands.43: A crowd at a village green watches two men wrestle for a ham, and invites the strongest-looking of you to try next.
heartlands.44: A row of graves along the road has fresh flowers on every one but the last.
heartlands.45: A girl rides past on a plough-horse with no saddle, waving a letter and shouting that the war is over; nobody believes her.
heartlands.46: An old stone circle stands in a sheep pasture, and the sheep will not graze inside it.
heartlands.47: A gang of reapers sits in the shade at noon sharing bread and cider, and offers you a mouthful if you can tell a good story.
heartlands.48: A gentleman's hunt crashes across the road after a fox, and the last rider shouts at you for being in the way.
heartlands.49: Bees drone in clover so thick and sweet that the whole meadow seems to hum.
heartlands.50: A rag tied to a gatepost marks a house with sickness inside, and the gate is chained shut.
heartlands.51: The ruts in the road are so deep that a cart has sunk to its axles, and the carter is cursing the Council of Many to the sky.
heartlands.52: A watermill stands still beside a dry millrace; the stream above it has simply stopped.
heartlands.53: An old woman sits outside her cottage shelling peas, and greets you as if you were her grandchildren come home at last.
heartlands.54: A pair of hares box in a field, oblivious to everything.
heartlands.55: A Conclave land-agent hammers a notice into a cottage door while the family stands silently in the garden.
heartlands.56: A distant church spire catches the sun and gleams, the only bright thing on the whole horizon.
heartlands.57: Wild roses tangle over a broken wall, and behind it lies the overgrown garden of a house that burned long ago.
heartlands.58: A cart of turnips has tipped into a ditch, and a dozen village children are helping themselves while the owner runs for help.
heartlands.59: A brook runs clear and cold across the road, and something glints among the pebbles at the bottom.
heartlands.60: A young man stands at a crossroads with his whole life in a bundle, unable to decide which way to go, and asks you to choose for him.
heartlands.61: Men are raising a maypole on a village green, though it is the wrong season, "to remind the sun what it is for".
heartlands.62: An ox has died in its yoke in the middle of a field, and the farmer sits beside it with his head in his hands.
heartlands.63: The wind combs the barley into long silver waves that run all the way to the hills.
heartlands.64: A packhorse train of salt merchants winds past, the bells on their harnesses ringing in no particular tune.
heartlands.65: A heron stands motionless in a flooded field, and does not move even when you pass close enough to touch it.
heartlands.66: A village has hung every door with a sprig of rowan; a man up a ladder is still adding them, and says it is "just in case".
heartlands.67: A wayshrine has been newly painted and its lamp freshly trimmed, though the village nearby is long empty.
heartlands.68: Somewhere beyond the hedges, a fiddler is playing a reel at a furious pace, and you never see where the music comes from.
heartlands.69: A plump priest rides past on a donkey, blessing everyone in reach, and asks for nothing in return but a little news.
heartlands.70: A field of sunflowers has turned, every head, to face the east, though it is late afternoon.
heartlands.71: A pig has escaped and runs squealing down the road, pursued by an entire family with brooms.
heartlands.72: A tall hay-rick has been built in the shape of a man, arms outstretched, and the villagers say it is for a festival.
heartlands.73: A lad on a wall throws a stone at a crow, misses, and shouts after it that it can tell its master he is not afraid.
heartlands.74: A pond reflects the sky perfectly, and in it the sun looks a little brighter than it does above.
heartlands.75: A drunk sleeps under a hedge with an empty jug, his boots set neatly side by side beside him.
heartlands.76: An inn courtyard is full of Conclave soldiers watering their horses, and their sergeant asks where you are bound and why.
heartlands.77: A young couple is carving their initials into an ancient beech, which already bears hundreds of others.
heartlands.78: A woman sells honey cakes from a basket at a crossroads, and will trade one for any song you can sing.
heartlands.79: Mist lies in the low meadows like milk, and only the tops of the hedges show above it.
heartlands.80: A group of Wardens is clearing a choked stream, and asks whether you can lend a hand with the stubborn root at the bottom.
heartlands.81: A gallows stands empty at the edge of a market town, freshly whitewashed for no clear reason.
heartlands.82: A ruined windmill turns slowly in the breeze, though it has no sails.
heartlands.83: The village bells ring out in celebration: a baby has been born at sunrise, and that is considered very lucky indeed.
heartlands.84: A traveller coming the other way warns you that the road ahead is watched, and will not say by whom.
heartlands.85: A scythe-maker's forge rings beside the road, and a row of new blades shines on the wall like teeth.
heartlands.86: An old soldier tends a little cottage garden and keeps his sword hung over the door, polished and ready.
heartlands.87: A farmer's daughter is reading a book on a stile, and hides it under her apron, flushing, as you come near.
heartlands.88: A row of beehives has been draped in black cloth; the beekeeper has died, and someone has told the bees.
heartlands.89: A great barn burns in the distance, and a line of tiny figures passes buckets from the pond.
heartlands.90: A herdsman whistles and his dog brings a whole flock round the hill in a single grey wave.
heartlands.91: The road is lined with stalls for a harvest fair, and a man in a sun mask is selling paper charms against the dark.
heartlands.92: A wagon of Conclave grain rolls past under armed guard, and the hungry faces at the roadside watch it all the way.
heartlands.93: An ancient yew shades a churchyard where the gravestones lean together like old friends gossiping.
heartlands.94: A girl selling eggs counts your change three times, then gives you one egg extra "for luck on the road".
heartlands.95: A field mouse runs across the path in front of you, stops, and stares, as if waiting for you to speak.
heartlands.96: The afternoon light lies gold and heavy on everything, and for once the world feels as if it might go on forever.
heartlands.97: A thatcher on a cottage roof calls down to ask the news from the city, and laughs at whatever you tell him.
heartlands.98: A line of washing has blown off a hedge and across the road: a christening gown, a shroud and a pair of bright red stockings.
heartlands.99: An old wellhead is garlanded with fresh flowers, and the village girls dare each other to whisper a wish down it.
heartlands.100: At a ford, a carter has stopped to let his horses drink, and he swears the water tastes sweeter here than anywhere else in the world.

hinterlands.1: A line of cairns marches over a ridge, and on the newest someone has set a child's shoe.
hinterlands.2: The salt-flats glare white beneath a thin, caustic sun, and your shadows look wrong, a little too long.
hinterlands.3: You pass the shell of a coaching inn, its sign still swinging: "The Last Welcome". A kettle inside is warm.
hinterlands.4: A scavenger crew crosses your path hauling a sledge piled with church bells, and offers to trade for water.
hinterlands.5: Wind hums through the ribs of something huge half-buried in the dunes.
hinterlands.6: A ruined town's well still has a bucket on its rope, and the rope has been cut and knotted back together many times.
hinterlands.7: Wild horses watch from a ridgeline, thin as rakes, and do not run when you come near.
hinterlands.8: A levy deserter in a ragged uniform asks which way the war is, so he can walk the other way.
hinterlands.9: A crow follows you for an hour, landing a little ahead each time, as if waiting for you to drop something.
hinterlands.10: A painted waystone marks the old road, its arrow pointing back the way you came.
hinterlands.11: A rusted troop-wagon lies on its side in a gully, and the bones inside are still in their seats.
hinterlands.12: Thorn bushes grow in rings here, each ring around a bare patch of earth where nothing will take root.
hinterlands.13: A cold wind brings the smell of the sea, though the nearest coast is weeks away.
hinterlands.14: On a hilltop, a single tower stands with a lamp still burning at its top, and no door at its foot.
hinterlands.15: Old fields lie fallow under a crust of grey frost, their boundary walls slowly sinking into the earth.
hinterlands.16: A woman with a rifle watches you from the porch of a lonely farmstead, and does not lower it until you are past.
hinterlands.17: Tattered prayer-flags of some forgotten order snap on poles along a high pass, faded to the colour of bone.
hinterlands.18: A dry riverbed winds across the plain, scattered with the hulls of boats that once sailed it.
hinterlands.19: A flock of carrion birds circles over something beyond the next rise, and their cries carry a long way in the still air.
hinterlands.20: You find a campfire still smouldering, with three bedrolls laid out beside it and no one in sight.
hinterlands.21: The ruins of a toll-house straddle the road, and someone has painted "PAY THE DEAD" across its gate.
hinterlands.22: A lone pilgrim walks the other way carrying a stone in each hand, and says he will set them on the last cairn he can find.
hinterlands.23: The wind has stripped a hillside back to old pavement: the streets of a town that was buried before anyone now living was born.
hinterlands.24: Wolves howl somewhere to the north, and an answering howl rises from the south, much closer.
hinterlands.25: A family of refugees huddles around a handcart on the roadside, asking whether Emberglow still takes in strangers.
hinterlands.26: A grove of dead trees stands white and leafless, each trunk carved with a name.
hinterlands.27: A collapsed bridge leaves you looking down at a river of grey ice groaning in its bed.
hinterlands.28: A gibbet creaks at a crossroads, its cage empty and its door hanging open.
hinterlands.29: The sun sits low and swollen on the horizon, and its light makes your eyes water and your skin prickle.
hinterlands.30: A gutted chapel stands in a field of nettles, and its bell rope moves gently, though there is no wind inside.
hinterlands.31: A mule wanders up to you fully laden with packs, its owner nowhere to be seen.
hinterlands.32: Snow has begun to fall, fine and grey, and it does not melt on your hands.
hinterlands.33: A hermit in a hide coat sits outside a cave and offers to read your fortune in the bones of a bird, for a single candle.
hinterlands.34: An old battlefield stretches across the plain, still scattered with rusting helmets that the frost pushes up each winter.
hinterlands.35: A signal tower on a distant hill flashes a message in mirror-light, and no tower answers it.
hinterlands.36: Salt crunches beneath your boots, and here and there the crust has broken over dark, oily water.
hinterlands.37: A whole herd of deer lies dead in a hollow without a mark on them, as if they simply lay down to sleep.
hinterlands.38: A scavenger has written warnings in chalk on a ruined wall, in a scrawl that grows shakier towards the end.
hinterlands.39: A cold mist creeps in at dusk, and voices in it call the names of people none of you know.
hinterlands.40: Tracks cross your path: big, clawed, and fresh, heading the same way you are going.
hinterlands.41: A ruined manor's gates still stand, and a stuffed bear in a moth-eaten coat stands guard on the drive.
hinterlands.42: An empty town still has its laundry out on the lines, faded and stiff, as if its people meant to come back for it.
hinterlands.43: A rope bridge spans a chasm, swaying in the wind, its planks newer at one end than the other.
hinterlands.44: You pass a peat-cutter's hut with the turf stacked neatly outside, and a pot of stew bubbling over the fire unattended.
hinterlands.45: Lightning flickers on the horizon without thunder, and the light it makes is faintly green.
hinterlands.46: A broken statue of some forgotten god lies face down in the road, and someone has carefully dressed its back in a cloak.
hinterlands.47: The road becomes a causeway across a black marsh, marked by poles topped with the skulls of animals.
hinterlands.48: A boy herding goats offers to guide you through the hills for a share of your food, and swears he knows a short cut.
hinterlands.49: A long-dead campfire is ringed with stones carved into little faces, all looking outward.
hinterlands.50: The ground trembles faintly underfoot for a minute, then is still, and the birds fall silent for an hour afterwards.
hinterlands.51: A bandit's head has been left on a stake beside the road with a sign: "He asked for a toll."
hinterlands.52: The plain is dotted with standing stones that seem to lean, each one, a little towards the north.
hinterlands.53: An old woman drives a cart pulled by a single huge dog, and asks if you have seen her son, who went to the cairns.
hinterlands.54: A cattle-drover's cross marks a grave by the road, and the dates carved on it are next year's.
hinterlands.55: The hills here are terraced for a vineyard long since gone wild, the grapes small, black and bitter.
hinterlands.56: You find a wooden doll sitting upright on a fence post, facing the way you came.
hinterlands.57: A rotting barge lies stranded miles from any water, its name still legible on the bow: "Hope of Emberglow".
hinterlands.58: Snow geese pass overhead in a great skein, flying south and calling, though it is the wrong time of year.
hinterlands.59: A shrine of piled antlers stands at a fork in the trail, hung with scraps of cloth and tarnished coins.
hinterlands.60: A dust devil whirls across the flats and collapses at your feet, leaving behind a little heap of grey ash.
hinterlands.61: Smoke rises from a village on the far hillside, but when you look again there is no village there, only rocks.
hinterlands.62: A wounded scavenger lies by the road clutching a sack, and begs you to take it to his sister in the Gaslake.
hinterlands.63: The light dims at midday as a vast cloud of starlings turns over the plain like smoke.
hinterlands.64: An old levy fort guards nothing now, its walls overgrown, its gate propped open with a cannon barrel.
hinterlands.65: A cold spring bubbles from the rocks, its water tasting faintly of iron and blood.
hinterlands.66: The road is cut by a ditch dug across it by hand, and the earth from it is piled into a wall facing the north.
hinterlands.67: A crew of Conclave surveyors hammers stakes into the frozen ground, mapping land that no one is left to farm.
hinterlands.68: A child's voice sings somewhere in the ruins of a mill, and stops the moment you call out.
hinterlands.69: Hailstones the size of marbles rattle down for a minute, then the sky clears as if nothing happened.
hinterlands.70: A great crack runs through the land, ten feet wide and black, and a cold breath rises from it.
hinterlands.71: A group of riders on shaggy ponies watches you from a distance all afternoon, never coming closer.
hinterlands.72: You find a battered trunk by the road full of fine dresses, neatly folded, and a letter addressed to no one.
hinterlands.73: The wind whistles through a ruined church organ whose pipes stand open to the sky, playing a low, endless chord.
hinterlands.74: A fox trots across your path carrying something shiny in its mouth, and looks back as if daring you to follow.
hinterlands.75: A thin, bitter rain begins to fall, and the drops leave pale spots on your clothes where they land.
hinterlands.76: A wooden palisade circles a hilltop, and from behind it comes the sound of hammering and children laughing.
hinterlands.77: A lone tree on the moor is hung with old lanterns, all of them cracked and empty.
hinterlands.78: A mudslide has buried the road, and sticking out of it is the hand of a stone statue, palm up.
hinterlands.79: At dusk the horizon to the north glows faintly, not like fire, more like the inside of a shell.
hinterlands.80: An old scavenger sits on a rock sorting through a heap of buttons, and says each one is from someone who did not come back.
hinterlands.81: A pack of feral dogs follows you at a distance, wearing the remains of collars.
hinterlands.82: A lake lies utterly still and mirror-black, and nothing at all is reflected in it.
hinterlands.83: A burnt-out caravan of wagons lies across the road, and the tracks of those who fled lead off in every direction.
hinterlands.84: A wanderer sells maps of the Hinterlands, and no two of them agree about anything except where the cairns are.
hinterlands.85: The frost has drawn ferns and stars on every stone, and they crunch like sugar underfoot.
hinterlands.86: A crumbling aqueduct strides across the valley, and water still drips from it, though it leads from nowhere.
hinterlands.87: You hear distant gunfire, two shots, then a long silence.
hinterlands.88: A broken cart wheel has been propped against a waymarker, and painted on it is a crude sun with a line through it.
hinterlands.89: The ground is spongy and warm here, and the grass is a startling green in the middle of the grey.
hinterlands.90: A tired old knight in rusted armour sits by the road and asks, quite seriously, whether his lord's castle still stands.
hinterlands.91: A stone hut by the trail has a sign: "Shelter. Take what you need. Leave what you can."
hinterlands.92: The sky turns a deep bruise-purple at sunset, and the sun seems to sink much faster than it should.
hinterlands.93: A broken mirror propped on a cairn catches your reflection, and it takes a moment too long to move.
hinterlands.94: A goatherd's pipe plays on the hills above you, a lonely tune that seems to come from a different direction each time.
hinterlands.95: A trapper's line of snares crosses your path, every one holding a hare that has been dead for weeks.
hinterlands.96: At the top of a rise you see the whole of the Hinterlands spread out grey and silent beneath you, and the dark line of the cairns at its far edge.
hinterlands.97: A half-buried bell sticks out of a sand dune, and when the wind is right it gives a single dull note.
hinterlands.98: A lone rider passes at a distance, wrapped in furs, leading a riderless horse with an empty saddle.
hinterlands.99: A ruined watchtower bears fresh graffiti from a levy patrol: names, dates, and a crude drawing of the cairns with an arrow and the word "soon".
hinterlands.100: A pair of vultures squabble over a scrap of red cloth on a thorn bush, and drop it at your feet when you come close.

darklands.1: Past the last cairn, your footsteps stop making a sound, though you can still feel the ground beneath them.
darklands.2: Your torch burns with a flame that leans away from the dark ahead, as if afraid of it.
darklands.3: A village stands whole and empty, its tables laid, and none of you can remember its name a moment after reading the sign.
darklands.4: The horizon is not black but missing, like a page torn from a book.
darklands.5: Snow falls upward, slowly, from the grey ground into the grey sky.
darklands.6: You find your own tracks ahead of you, going the way you are going.
darklands.7: A bell tolls somewhere far off, and each stroke is fainter than the last, though you walk towards it.
darklands.8: One of you suddenly cannot remember their mother's face, and then, a moment later, they can.
darklands.9: An old cairn-builder sits on a stone, carefully stacking rocks, and says the dark moved a mile last night.
darklands.10: Colour drains from your clothes as you walk, and returns only when you look back the way you came.
darklands.11: A road runs on ahead, perfectly paved, and simply ends in mid-air at the edge of nothing.
darklands.12: The wind has stopped, and the silence is so complete that you can hear each other's hearts.
darklands.13: A house stands alone with its door open and a fire lit in the hearth, giving no warmth at all.
darklands.14: Your breath does not mist in the cold; it simply vanishes as it leaves your lips.
darklands.15: A tree grows here with leaves of grey paper, each covered in handwriting too faded to read.
darklands.16: Something vast passes overhead, blotting out what little light there is, and makes no sound at all.
darklands.17: A dead traveller sits against a cairn, perfectly preserved, with a smile on his face and his eyes closed.
darklands.18: The ground underfoot changes from earth to stone to something smooth and cold, like glass that is not quite there.
darklands.19: You hear someone calling your name in your own voice.
darklands.20: The stars here are wrong: too few, too close, and none of them twinkle.
darklands.21: A rope is staked into the ground and runs out into the dark, taut, as if someone at the far end is still holding it.
darklands.22: Your shadows have gone. When you look for them, there is only bare grey earth around your feet.
darklands.23: A field of grave markers stretches ahead, all blank, all freshly cut.
darklands.24: Your torches gutter and shrink to blue points for a long moment, then flare up again as if nothing happened.
darklands.25: A child's swing hangs from nothing, moving gently back and forth.
darklands.26: The air tastes of old pennies and cold ash, and it is hard to get a full breath.
darklands.27: A lantern hangs from a pole beside the path, burning with a black flame that makes the dark around it deeper.
darklands.28: You come upon a perfect copy of the last inn you slept in, every detail right, except that the windows show only darkness.
darklands.29: The sound of the sea comes from all around you, though there is no water anywhere.
darklands.30: A wall of grey fog stands ahead, flat and still as a curtain, and the cold coming off it numbs your faces.
darklands.31: A shape stands in the distance, too still to be alive and too tall to be a man, and it is closer each time you look up.
darklands.32: The path is littered with things travellers dropped: a boot, a book, a doll, a sword, all half sunk into the ground.
darklands.33: You pass a signpost where every arm reads the same word, scratched out.
darklands.34: A faint music drifts on the air, a waltz played on a music box that is winding down.
darklands.35: The rocks here have been worn smooth into the shapes of faces, all turned towards the void.
darklands.36: For a moment, all of you forget why you came here, and stand in silence until one of you remembers.
darklands.37: A great hole yawns beside the path, and from it rises the sound of distant, endless falling.
darklands.38: The cold is not like winter cold; it seems to come from inside your bones and work its way outward.
darklands.39: A crowd of grey figures stands motionless on a hillside, facing away, and none of them turns at your approach.
darklands.40: Your rations taste of nothing, and the water in your flasks has gone flat and lifeless.
darklands.41: You find a cairn that someone has started building from the far side, facing the world of light.
darklands.42: A pale glow on the horizon looks like dawn, but it never grows brighter, however long you watch.
darklands.43: A single flower grows from the bare earth, perfectly white, and it closes as you pass.
darklands.44: The ground is covered with a fine grey dust that rises at each step and hangs in the air behind you like a trail.
darklands.45: You hear a dog barking far behind you, back towards the world, and the sound is unbearably comforting.
darklands.46: An empty cradle rocks gently in the middle of the road.
darklands.47: A broken lantern lies at your feet, and when one of you picks it up, it is still warm.
darklands.48: The dark ahead seems to breathe, very slowly, drawing in a little closer with each breath.
darklands.49: Writing appears in the frost on a stone: the names of your party, one by one, then fading.
darklands.50: An old map in your pack has changed: the land behind you is drawn in, but the land ahead is now bare paper.
darklands.51: A tall door stands alone in the waste, closed, with light showing under it.
darklands.52: Your voices sound thin and far away, as though you were shouting from the bottom of a well.
darklands.53: Birds lie dead in a neat line across the path, as if they had flown into a wall that is not there.
darklands.54: The pale sun shows through the gloom as a hollow ring, with darkness at its heart.
darklands.55: A traveller passes you going the other way, at a run, and does not stop or speak, and his footprints fade behind him.
darklands.56: A circle of ash on the ground marks where a camp was made, and inside it lie the cinders of a fire that burned black.
darklands.57: One of you finds a coin in their pocket from a country none of you has ever heard of.
darklands.58: The wind returns all at once, howling, and carries whispers in it that almost make words.
darklands.59: A church steeple rises from the grey earth up to its belfry, as if the rest of the church were buried, or swallowed.
darklands.60: The memory of the last good meal you ate comes to each of you unbidden, so vivid that you can taste it.
darklands.61: Long strips of cloth tied to cairns stream towards the dark, all pulled the same way, though the air is still.
darklands.62: A pool of water shows a clear blue sky in its reflection, though the sky above you is grey and starless.
darklands.63: Nothing grows here; even the lichen on the stones is dead and peeling.
darklands.64: Hoofbeats approach from behind at a gallop, louder and louder, then pass right through you and fade ahead.
darklands.65: A tall cairn here has been knocked down, and its stones lie scattered as if kicked by something enormous.
darklands.66: You can no longer tell how long you have been walking, and no one's guess agrees.
darklands.67: An old man sits at a table in the open, playing a board game against an empty chair, and invites one of you to take the other side.
darklands.68: The faint outline of a city glimmers ahead like a mirage, all towers and lit windows, and fades when you come near.
darklands.69: A trail of footprints leads into the dark, and none comes back.
darklands.70: Your torchlight seems to stop a few feet ahead of you, as if it hits a wall of black glass.
darklands.71: A drift of moths settles on your clothes, grey and soft, and dies there without a flutter.
darklands.72: One of you hears a lullaby they have not heard since childhood, sung very softly, just behind their ear.
darklands.73: The ground is warm here, unnervingly warm, like the flank of something sleeping.
darklands.74: A cairn bears a plaque: "The edge of the world, as of the year 702." It is a long way behind the true edge.
darklands.75: Fragments of things float in the air at shoulder height: a teacup, a page, a lock of hair, turning slowly.
darklands.76: You stumble on the remains of an old camp of explorers, their journals open, every page filled with the same sentence.
darklands.77: A deep note sounds, below hearing, felt in your teeth and stomach rather than your ears.
darklands.78: The darkness to the north has edges, like a coastline, and you can see it eating away at the land very slowly.
darklands.79: A trickle of sand runs uphill across the path.
darklands.80: Something has left gifts by the path: a ribbon, a ring, a lock of grey hair, each on its own flat stone.
darklands.81: One of the party's names will not come to anyone's lips for a full minute, until it suddenly returns.
darklands.82: The silence is broken by a single sob somewhere close by, and then by nothing at all.
darklands.83: Your torch smoke does not rise; it pours down and spreads along the ground like water.
darklands.84: A field of standing stones turns out, on closer look, to be people turned grey and still, mid-stride, all walking into the dark.
darklands.85: You catch the smell of fresh bread and summer rain, so strong and sudden that one of you cries out.
darklands.86: A huge eye seems to open in the dark above the horizon, and slowly closes again.
darklands.87: Every sound you make comes back to you a moment later, a little quieter and a little wrong.
darklands.88: A grey hare sits upright in the path and watches you with eyes like holes, then is simply gone.
darklands.89: Ahead, the land crumbles at its edges into motes of dust that drift away into nothing.
darklands.90: A last cairn-keeper's lantern hangs from a hook driven into the bare rock, and its oil is nearly spent.
darklands.91: For one moment, the light comes back: colour, warmth, birdsong. Then it is gone, and the dark feels heavier than before.
darklands.92: Your hands look faintly translucent in the gloom, and the feeling passes only when you are back in torchlight.
darklands.93: Someone has scratched a message into a flat rock: "Turn back. It does not end. It only stops."
darklands.94: The sky above is a vast, empty grey, without sun, moon, cloud or star, and it seems very close.
darklands.95: You look back, and the cairns behind you are much further away than you thought.
darklands.96: A garden grows here in perfect rows of grey cabbages and grey roses, tended by no one, smelling of nothing.
darklands.97: A wooden boat sits on the bare ground, oars shipped, as if waiting for a tide that will never come.
darklands.98: You pass a cairn hung with keys of every size, hundreds of them, and none of them makes a sound in the wind.
darklands.99: A thin line of light on the ground leads ahead, like the glow under a door, and it goes out the moment someone steps on it.
darklands.100: Far behind you, a single cock crows, and the dark around you shivers very slightly.

Minion.Made: {item}: {name} is now {owner}’s {tier}. Pick its abilities with the Dark Master and write them on its sheet.
Minion.AskDm: {item}: making a minion needs the right to create actors. Ask the Dark Master to press the Use button.

TierAbilities.moderate: one passive and one ◈◈ active ability

Minion.TierHint: This tier: HP {hp}, Morale {morale}, armour {armour}, attack {attack}, {abilities} (rules 3.14).
Minion.ApplyTierAsk: Set HP, Morale, armour and the first attack's damage to those of a {tier}? What is there now is replaced.
Minion.OwnerHint: The character it serves. A character can have minions up to their Presence (minimum 1); an owner already at the limit is refused. The owner's players can command it and roll for it.
Minion.RulesHint: A minion has 2 actions and 0 reactions, and acts only when commanded (◈). It tests, attacks and defends at +0, has no Fortune and no wounds, and dies at 0 HP. In combat it acts right after its owner.
Minion.MoraleHint: Roll 2d6: above its Morale, the minion is demoralised. Morale – never rolls.
Minion.ArmourHint: Subtracted from damage that hits the minion. A defence Ruin steps it down one.
Minion.AttackTooltip: Attack at +0: opens the attack dialogue
Minion.DropHint: Drag weapons (attacks) and feats (passives and active abilities) from the Items sidebar onto this sheet, or use the Add buttons.
Minion.Heading: Minions ({count}/{limit})
Minion.LimitHint: You can have minions up to your Presence (minimum 1). Every minion counts, summoned ones too (rules 3.14).
Minion.NoneYet: None. Give a minion this character as its owner on the minion's sheet.
Minion.CommandTooltip: Command a minion (◈): in combat, on your own turn, spend one action. Its turn, right after yours, has two actions.
Minion.OverLimit: {owner} already has {limit} minions, their limit (Presence, minimum 1). Dismiss, release or abandon one before {name} can join.
Minion.NotYourTurn: You can only command a minion on your own turn.
Minion.NotInCombat: {name} is not in this combat. Add its token to the Combat Tracker first.
Minion.NotYours: You do not own {name}. Ask the Dark Master to give it an owner on its sheet.
Minion.AlreadyCommanded: {name} has already been commanded for its next turn.
Minion.NoActions: No actions left this turn. The command is given anyway; the Dark Master decides.
Minion.Commanded: {owner} commands {name} (◈). It acts right after {owner}, with two actions.
Minion.TurnIdle: {name} was not commanded by {owner}: no actions. It only acts to escape obvious harm.
Minion.Fell: {name} falls at 0 HP and is dead.

Relic.SheetHint: The Description box below is the relic's effect. Every relic has the Expendable d20 trait: after each use roll a d20, and on a 1 it is used up (rules 4.2).
Relic.AlwaysOnHint: Its effect is always on, like the rebreather or the compass. Instead of Use it has a Daily roll: the Expendable d20, once per day, the first time its effect matters.
Relic.EmberGainHint: Added to the Ember pool when the relic is used, such as 3 for the Shard of the Great Brazier. Only in combat, as there is no pool outside it. Leave at 0 for none.
Relic.DestroyedHint: Used up or burnt out by its Last Rite: its drawback applies. Untick it when the relic is recovered; it can then be used again.
Relic.DestroyedTooltip: Destroyed. Untick Destroyed on the relic if it is recovered.
Relic.SaleValueHint: What a fence or collector pays. Its drawback strikes the moment it leaves your hands.
Relic.FactionValueHint: What its faction pays to take it home. Then the drawback does not apply.
Relic.DrawbackHint: This relic is destroyed, so its drawback applies until it is recovered.
Relic.UseTooltip: Use it: posts its effect, then rolls the Expendable d20
Relic.DailyTooltip: Daily roll: the Expendable d20, the first time today its effect matters
Relic.LastRiteTooltip: Last Rite: it always works, needs no ember and no Expendable roll, and destroys the relic
Relic.UsedUp: Used up: the relic is destroyed!
Relic.IsDestroyed: {item} is destroyed. Untick Destroyed on it if it is recovered.
Relic.NeedsCombat: {item} adds to the Ember pool, and there is no pool outside combat.
Relic.LastRiteAsk: Burn {item} out for its Last Rite? It always works, and the relic is destroyed.
Relic.LastRiteRule: A Last Rite always works, needs no ember and no Expendable roll.
Relic.BurntOut: The relic is burnt out and destroyed.
Relic.RecoverHint: If it is recovered, the Dark Master unticks Destroyed on the relic.

Class.Hint: You begin with your class feature and class power, and nothing more (rules 2.5); both are set by the class and added with it. The class's other feats and powers are earned through Improving.

Class.NotFound: {name} is not in the compendiums: add it by hand.

Equipment.DogMissing: The small vicious dog is not added: the Dark Master adds it as a minion (Import examples has one).
Equipment.VehicleAdded: {vehicle} now belongs to {name}: find it in the Actors sidebar.

Lasting.HiddenHint: Only the Dark Master sees the area on the map, like a hidden bear trap.

Lasting.PersistentThreat: {name} is caught in {area}: defend (Agility DR12) or take {formula} persistent {type} damage.

Area.NoToken: {name} has no token on this scene: target the creatures in the area by hand.
Area.Aim: {name}: place the area and left-click. Right-click or Escape cancels.
Area.NoGM: A Dark Master must be connected for this area to stay on the map.
Area.KeepFailed: The area could not be placed on the map. Ask the Dark Master to check the console.
Area.TooFar: Too far: {feet} ft, and the range is {range} ft.
Area.SheetHint: When it is used, the area is placed on the map and every creature it covers at least half of becomes a target (rules: Areas of Effect).
Area.SizeHint: The radius of an emanation or burst; the length of a cone, line or wall; the side of a square.
Area.RangeHint: How far away the burst's or square's point may be. 0 for no limit.
Area.IncludesUserHint: The user is caught in their own area ("you included").
Area.Hint: An area: every targeted creature shares the one damage roll. Foes take it with Inflict damage (their armour soaks); characters and minions defend.
Area.SharedGloom: Damage rolled once for every target: {rolls}.
Area.TossHint: Used by tossing it: aim at a point within its range, then test Agility DR12. Triumph or Success: it lands there; Failure: it misses; Ruin: it lands at your feet (rules 4.1, Bombs).
Area.SuccessSizeHint: The area's size on a Success or Ruin, such as a grenade's 5' burst. 0 for the same size on every result.

Outcome.Title: What it gives
Outcome.TitleHint: What each result gives the targeted creatures or the user, given by itself when the card is posted and changed if Fortune changes the result.
Outcome.None: Nothing set: its text is on the card.

Kind.heal: Healing (an amount, full, or damage: as much as the card's damage)
Kind.subject: Becomes the subject

Outcome.DurationHint: How long a condition or buff lasts. On the user of a Sustained power: until the power ends.
Outcome.BuffEffectsHint: The effects a buff gives the creature while it lasts, as a temporary item named after the power.
Outcome.NoGM: No Dark Master is connected to change a creature you do not own.
Outcome.SoakedHint: Tick when armour soaks this damage. Unticked: nothing reduces it.
Outcome.NextOnlyHint: On a foe: ends after its next attack has been defended against. On a character: ends after the first roll it helps.
Outcome.OptionHint: The option this belongs to, such as Allegro. Leave empty for always. The power dialogue asks which option.
Outcome.TriumphPicksHint: How many options a Triumph lets the user choose (Daring Stunt: 2).
Outcome.ArmourLowered: {name}'s armour drops from {from} to {to} until the encounter ends.
Outcome.Partner: {name} is {user}'s dance partner until the encounter ends.
Outcome.NoPartner: {power}: no dance partner is named this encounter.
Outcome.EffectOptionHint: Only for the buff of this option, such as Hardened Keratin. Leave empty for every option.
Outcome.NoRig: {name} has no rig aboard: apply the damage by hand.
Outcome.ThrallsAskHint: {have} thrall(s). Each adds {per} damage, up to {max}.
Outcome.Quarry: {name} is {user}'s quarry until the encounter ends.
Outcome.Subject: {name} is {user}'s subject until the encounter ends.
Outcome.TestHint: Ticked: the usual Toughness DR12 test follows, as for life force (Overcharge). Unticked: no test (Crimson bargain).
Outcome.Wound: {name} gains a wound ({wounds}/{max}), with no Table of Agony.
Outcome.WoundTest: {name} gains a wound ({wounds}/{max}) and tests Toughness.
Outcome.WoundAtMax: {name} is at maximum wounds: no wound is added.
Outcome.WhileSustainedHint: The condition lasts while the spell or power is sustained, and ends on every target when it ends.

Ongoing.Title: Ongoing
Ongoing.NotYours: Only this creature's owner or the Dark Master can change its effects.

Hint.cover: Left click: heavier cover. Right click: lighter cover, then none.
Hint.light: Right click: dim a lantern, then put the light out (it is spent). Left click: turn a dimmed lantern back up.

Ongoing.Collapse: Hide the names of ongoing effects
Ongoing.Expand: Ongoing conditions and effects: show their names
Ongoing.NoneOther: No other ongoing effects. Conditions are listed below.
Ongoing.UntilTurn: until the start of your next turn
Ongoing.InDarknessText: No light reaches you: Bane on all tests, attacks and defences. Ends when a light reaches you.

Cover.Title: {name} takes cover
Cover.Ask: How good is the cover? Light: a wooden door, an overturned table. Heavy: a stone pillar.
Cover.Taken: {name} takes {size} cover: {dr} DR to defend until the start of their next turn.
Cover.NotYourTurn: In combat you can only take cover on your own turn.
Cover.NoActions: No actions left this turn. Cover is taken anyway; the Dark Master decides.
Cover.Damaged: Only the cover stopped the blow: it strikes the cover, which is now light cover.
Cover.Destroyed: Only the cover stopped the blow: it strikes the cover, which is destroyed.

Manual.Title: Basic actions

Tooltip.attack: Attack ◈: pick a weapon at hand and attack.
Tooltip.defend: Defend: test Agility DR12 against an attack that has no foe card. You give the damage.
Tooltip.command: Command a minion ◈: it gets two actions this turn.
Tooltip.improvise: Improvise ◈–◈◈◈: anything outside the rules. The Dark Master may ask for Tests or more actions.
Tooltip.interact: Interact ◈–◈◈◈: use an object, draw a weapon, pry open a door.
Tooltip.cast: Cast a spell ◈–◈◈◈: a Sanity Test (rules 3.11).
Tooltip.sustain: Sustain ◈: keep one Sustained spell or power going until your next turn.
Tooltip.cover: Take cover ◈: duck behind something on the map. Light cover −2 DR, heavy cover −4 DR to defend, until the start of your next turn.

Nothing.attack: {name} has no weapon at hand (equipped or carried loose).

Manual.DefendDamageHint: Dice such as d6 or 2d4, or a number such as 3. Rolled only if you are hit.
Manual.BadDamage: “{damage}” is not damage: write dice such as d6, or a number.

Hint.improvise: Anything outside the rules. The Dark Master may ask for Tests or more actions.
Hint.interact: Use an object, draw your weapon, pry open a door.

Manual.NotYourTurn: In combat, you can only do this on your own turn.
Manual.NoActions: No actions left this turn; spent anyway.

Encounter.Title: Encounter builder

Feel.easy: A scuffle in the soot. Costs a little HP, maybe a torch.
Feel.standard: A real fight. Someone will bleed.
Feel.hard: The wick burns low. Expect a wound or a fallen PC.
Feel.deadly: A boss, or a slaughter. Someone may not walk out.

Encounter.DarkHint: A Standard fight in the dark, with no light to see by, plays as a Hard one. Terrain and surprise can raise a fight a full step.
Encounter.RollCategoryTooltip: Roll the d10 Type of creature table and tick what it gives.
Encounter.NoCategory: Tick at least one category of foe.
Encounter.Heading: {difficulty} encounter for {players} players: {type}
Encounter.RollsAgain: d6: {rolls} (rolled again until it fitted the party)
Encounter.NotFit: No result on this table fits the budget for this party, so the foes are over budget. With fewer than four players, a foe this strong is a fight to survive, not to win: make sure the players can see a way out.
Encounter.Missing: The ticked categories have no foe of some tiers. Tick another category and reroll that place.
Encounter.MissingWarn: Some places have no foe: the ticked categories have none of that tier.
Encounter.RerollTooltip: Pick another foe of this tier
Encounter.NoScene: There is no scene to place the foes on.

FoeLoot.Hint: What the foe carries. Loot is set aside: a weapon here is not an attack, and its effects are off. When the foe drops to 0 HP, its loot and silver drop in a chest on its square.
FoeLoot.SpoilsTooltip: Search the fallen (rules 5): roll a d6. 1–3 nothing worth taking, 4–5 d10 s, 6 one roll on the Spoils table. Beasts carry nothing; every other foe is searched.
FoeLoot.DropHint: Drag items onto this section to make them loot.
FoeLoot.Heading: Searching {name}
FoeLoot.SpoilsRoll: d6 {d6}: one roll on the Spoils table.
FoeLoot.Beast: {name} is a beast and carries nothing, though a Ranger or Scholar may harvest it.
FoeLoot.Dropped: {name} dropped its loot in a chest on its square.

Treasure.Title: Treasure

Size.small: Small: a cellar, a tomb, a smugglers' hole (1–3 encounters)
Size.medium: Medium: a ruined chapel, a warehouse, a bandit camp (4–6 encounters)
Size.large: Large: a drowned monastery, a foundry, a fortified keep (7–10 encounters)
Size.lair: Lair: the home of a Strong or Mighty foe

Region.deep: The Hinterlands or beyond the cairn-lights (double coin, one more Spoils roll)
Region.picked: The Heartlands or inside Emberglow (half coin)

RegionShort.deep: Where the dark is deeper: double coin, one more Spoils roll

Treasure.Mighty: A Mighty foe's lair (adds a spell tome)
Treasure.Hint: Rolled once for the whole site, for a party of four. Scatter it through the rooms, bodies and hiding places.
Treasure.Heading: Treasure: {size}
Treasure.Nothing: Nothing but bones, rags and a bad smell.
Treasure.Again: roll twice more on this table.
Treasure.TrinketText: A trinket: fetches 1–10 s from a curious buyer.
Treasure.ValuableText: A valuable: sells for its price.
Treasure.TomeText: A spell tome teaches the spell permanently after a Downtime of study, or can be read aloud once like a scroll.
Treasure.NoScene: There is no scene to place the treasure on.

ChatRolls.TestTooltip: Roll an ability test for your character
ChatRolls.PickHint: Choose the ability to test. You set the DR, Boon and Bane next.
ChatRolls.NoCharacter: Select your character's token, or choose a character for yourself in User Configuration.

Journal.Subtitle: Subtitle
Journal.SubtitleHint: A line under the heading, such as a date

FieldJournal.Name: Field notes: {name}
FieldJournal.NeedGM: The Dark Master must be logged in to start the field journal. The kind is still recorded on the feat.
FieldJournal.AutoRecorded: {item}: studied this encounter, now recorded: {kinds}. Notes: {list}.

Toss.Landed: {name}'s {item} lands where it was aimed ({size} ft).
Toss.AtFeet: {name} drops the {item}: it goes off at their feet ({size} ft).
Toss.ByHand: No token on this scene: target the creatures caught by hand.

Arcana.Heading: Your reading
Arcana.Empty: No reading yet. It is laid out after each Long Rest.
Arcana.AlreadyLaid: You already have a reading. A new one is laid out after your next Long Rest.
Arcana.TurnTooltip: Turn it for the targeted creature, or yourself with nothing targeted (↻, once per round)
Arcana.OncePerRound: You have already turned a card this round.
Arcana.NoReaction: Turning a card uses your reaction, and you have none left. Turning it anyway; the Dark Master decides.
Arcana.UsedReaction: Used the reaction to turn it.
Arcana.FortuneByGM: {name} gains {amount} Fortune (the Dark Master adds it: you do not own them).
Arcana.ByHand: Apply the rest of its meaning by hand.

forgeHeart.Name: The Forge-Heart
forgeHeart.Meaning: Their next weapon hit deals +d4 damage.

architect.Name: The Architect
architect.Meaning: They have light cover until the start of your next turn.

coldEye.Name: The Cold Eye
coldEye.Meaning: They defend with -2 DR until the start of your next turn.

wheel.Name: The Wheel
wheel.Meaning: Turn it after they roll a test: they reroll it and must keep the second result.

mask.Name: The Mask
mask.Meaning: For their next test, they may use Presence instead of the ability called for.

shade.Name: The Shade
shade.Meaning: Their next hit deals maximum damage, and they take d4 dark damage.

thirteenth.Name: The Thirteenth
thirteenth.Meaning: Black and blank. You cannot turn it. Once before your next Long Rest, the Dark Master may turn it: you or an ally within 30' makes one test with Bane.

Arcana.Foreseen: Foreseen: the first card of this combat uses no reaction.
Arcana.NotYourTurn: Shuffling the fates uses an action, so in combat you can only do it on your own turn.
Arcana.ShuffleTooltip: Draw every unturned card anew, except the Thirteenth (an action, once per Long Rest)
Arcana.ReverseTooltip: Reversed: turn it against the targeted foe; its meaning is lost, and the next attack against that foe has Boon (↻)
Arcana.ReverseNoFoe: Target a foe to turn a card against it.
Arcana.ReversedNote: the next attack against it has Boon
Arcana.TearTooltip: Black sector: tear the Thirteenth in half; you take d4 mental damage
Arcana.DmTooltip: Dark Master: turn the Thirteenth; the creature you target (or the Cartomancer) makes its next test with Bane
Arcana.DmTitle: The Thirteenth is turned: {name} makes the next test with Bane
Arcana.ThirteenthIn: The black card falls out of the deck: the Thirteenth replaces an unturned card of your reading.
Arcana.Doomed: {name}'s fate is sealed: at the end of each of its turns this encounter, the Dark Master rolls a d6.
Arcana.ThirteenthLocked: The Thirteenth enters your reading, and cannot be torn until your next Long Rest.
Arcana.DoomRoll: The Thirteenth card: {name} rolls {total} on the d6.
Arcana.DoomMighty: A 1: {name} is Mighty, and takes {amount} spirit damage instead of dying.
